questions.cardText:
[Zoology] What is the likely cause of some underground crayfish having bright colors?
A. Evolutionary accident
B. To attract mates
C. To blend in with their environment
Answer: A. According to recent research, environmental changes and genetic mutations likely led to the development of their vivid coloration, even though it may not provide a specific survival advantage in their subterranean habitats.
questions.de: Was erklärt laut einer Studie von 2024 wahrscheinlich die leuchtenden Farben grabender Flusskrebse, die ihnen unter der Erde keinen erkennbaren Vorteil bringen?
questions.en: According to a 2024 study, what likely explains the bright colours of burrowing crayfish, which give them no apparent advantage underground?
questions.answerDe: Zufall: durch genetische Drift fixierte Farbmutationen (ein evolutionärer Zufall)
questions.answerEn: Chance: colour mutations fixed by genetic drift (an evolutionary accident)

timeline.labelEn: Graham and Padilla Perez publish that bright colour in burrowing crayfish is probably neutral, not adaptive
timeline.labelDe: Graham und Padilla Perez veröffentlichen, dass die leuchtende Farbe grabender Flusskrebse wohl neutral und nicht adaptiv ist

source.title: Bright coloration in crayfish does not serve an evolutionary purpose

questions.notes: Card broadly right. The study (Zackary Graham & Dylan Padilla Perez, Proceedings of the Royal Society B, 2024) found bright colours evolved 50+ times, mostly in semi-terrestrial burrowing species, and proposes they are neutral: small, isolated populations let colour mutations become fixed by chance. The card’s “environmental changes” is not their claim, and the paper calls neutrality a hypothesis.

questions.cardText:
[Art History] Who painted “The Persistence of Memory,” known for its melting clocks?
A. Pablo Picasso
B. Vincent van Gogh
C. Salvador Dalí
Answer: C.
questions.de: Wer malte „Die Beständigkeit der Erinnerung“, bekannt für ihre zerfließenden Uhren?
